guides.name: Smoke alarm chirps every minute
steps: Listen: one short chirp every 30 to 60 seconds means a low battery.
Get a step stool with a handle bar. Never stand on a chair.
Take the alarm off its ceiling bracket, or open its battery door.
Sealed 10-year alarm? Its battery can't be changed. Replace the whole alarm.
Put in a new battery of the type the maker recommends.
Snap the battery in firmly and close the battery door all the way.
Put the alarm back and press the test button. It should sound loudly.
Still chirping? Take the battery out, hold the test button 15 seconds, then put it back.
Check the date on the back. Ten years old or more? Replace the whole alarm.
safety: On an alarm wired into the house, turn off its circuit breaker before taking it off the bracket.
Wired-in alarms have a backup battery too; replace it at least once a year.
stopIf: Three loud beeps and a pause means smoke. Get out and call 911 from outside.
It does not sound when you press test, even with a new battery. Replace the alarm.
It still chirps after a new battery and a reset. Replace the alarm.
A wired-in alarm chirps when another appliance turns on. Have an electrician check it.

sources.title: What Causes Consistent Chirping? | Kidde
sources.quote: Low Battery – The alarm will chirp every 30-40 seconds (every 60 seconds for some alarms) for a minimum of seven days. Replace the battery when this occurs, then test your alarm.

sources.title: What Causes Consistent Chirping? | Kidde
sources.quote: End of Life Condition (Sealed Battery Models Only) – The alarm will chirp every 30 seconds to indicate it is time to replace the alarm.

sources.title: What Causes Consistent Chirping? | Kidde
sources.quote: If the alarm does not sound, your unit has a defective battery or other failure.

sources.title: What Causes Intermittent Beeping or Chirping? | Kidde
sources.quote: Check the Battery Type: Ensure you have the recommended type of battery securely installed.

sources.title: What Causes Intermittent Beeping or Chirping? | Kidde
sources.quote: Secure the Battery: Make sure the battery is snapped in completely so it cannot be shaken loose.

sources.title: What Causes Intermittent Beeping or Chirping? | Kidde
sources.quote: Close the Battery Compartment: On units with a front-load battery, ensure the battery compartment door is closed completely.

sources.title: What Causes Intermittent Beeping or Chirping? | Kidde
sources.quote: Turn off the power to the smoke alarm at the circuit breaker. Remove the smoke alarm from the mounting bracket and disconnect the power.

sources.title: What Causes Intermittent Beeping or Chirping? | Kidde
sources.quote: Sometimes, the alarm's processor retains error conditions, such as a weak battery, even after the battery is replaced.

sources.title: What Causes Intermittent Beeping or Chirping? | Kidde
sources.quote: Remove the battery. Press and hold the test button for at least 15 seconds. The unit may chirp or alarm for a few seconds before going silent.

sources.title: What Causes Intermittent Beeping or Chirping? | Kidde
sources.quote: Smoke and heat alarms should be replaced every 10 years, and carbon monoxide and combination alarms every 7 years. Check the date code on the label attached to the back of the unit.

sources.title: What Causes Intermittent Beeping or Chirping? | Kidde
sources.quote: If none of these conditions apply and the suggestions don't help, it might be time to replace the alarm.

sources.title: What Causes Intermittent Beeping or Chirping? | Kidde
sources.quote: Check if the chirping occurs when something else in the house is turned on, like an exhaust fan or heater. If so, move the device to another outlet on a different circuit or have an electrician investigate.

sources.title: Why Do Smoke Alarms Always Chirp in the Middle of the Night? | Kidde
sources.quote: Kidde recommends replacing all smoke alarms—battery and hardwired—every 10 years. If your alarms are older or you don't know their age, you should replace them.

sources.title: Why Is My Smoke Detector Beeping | Fire Alarm Chirping | First Alert
sources.quote: If your smoke detector is beeping 3 times, you and your family need to evacuate and call 9-1-1 once safely outside.

sources.title: Why Is My Smoke Detector Beeping | Fire Alarm Chirping | First Alert
sources.quote: Ten-year sealed battery smoke alarms on the other hand do not require battery replacements, but should still be tested regularly.

sources.title: Why Is My Smoke Detector Beeping | Fire Alarm Chirping | First Alert
sources.quote: No matter the type of smoke alarm, all alarms should be replaced at least every 10 years from the manufacture date on the back of the alarm.

sources.title: Smoke Alarms | U.S. Fire Administration
sources.quote: Replace the backup battery at least once every year.

sources.title: Smoke Alarms | U.S. Fire Administration
sources.quote: Replace the entire smoke alarm every 10 years.

sources.title: Fire Safety for Older Adults (FA-221) | U.S. Fire Administration
sources.quote: Replace the entire smoke alarm every 10 years or sooner if it does not sound when you push the test button.

sources.title: Check for Safety: A Home Fall Prevention Checklist for Older Adults | CDC STEADI
sources.quote: If you must use a step stool, get one with a bar to hold on to. Never use a chair as a step stool.

guides.name: Recaulk a bathtub or shower
steps: Cut along both edges of the old caulk and peel or scrape all of it out.
Clean the joint with rubbing alcohol and let it dry completely.
Put painter's tape on both sides of the joint for a straight line.
Cut the tip at an angle and run one steady bead along the joint.
Smooth it with the tool, then pull the tape off right away.
Keep water off it for 24 hours so it cures.
safety: Use plastic scrapers on acrylic or fiberglass tubs to avoid scratches.
stopIf: The wall behind the old caulk is soft, moldy or wet.
Tiles are loose or the tub moves when you step in.

sources.title: How to recaulk your bathtub for a fresh, mold-free finish - GE Sealants
sources.quote: Moisture under fresh sealant ruins adhesion and invites mold later.

guides.name: Replace torn window screen mesh
steps: Lay the frame flat, pry out the old spline and remove the torn mesh.
Match the new spline size to the groove (bring a piece of the old one).
Tape the frame down and lay new mesh over it with extra on every side.
Roll the spline into the groove over the mesh, keeping the mesh square and snug.
Push the spline into the corners with a screwdriver tip.
Trim extra mesh along the outer edge of the groove with the knife.
safety: Cut away from your hand and change dull blades.
stopIf: The frame is bent, cracked or the corners are loose.
The screen is on an upper floor you can't remove from inside.

sources.title: How to Replace or Repair a Window or Door Screen | Phifer
sources.quote: Lay screen fabric over frame, align squarely and overlap 1/2” (1.3 cm) on all sides.
